text: Neutral standards-layer map as of 2026-09-05, covering verified shipping specifications, well-known artifacts, standards-track and individual drafts, and explicitly marked conventions and thin proposals. ACP names are separated by owner and function; ARD’s verified catalog path is /.well-known/ai-catalog.json, not ard.json. “NOT FOUND” identifies rows where a distinct dated adoption source could not be verified.

protocols.name: Model Context Protocol
protocols.adoption_evidence: Canonical 2026-07-28 specification release; used as the tool/context protocol by the Apps SDK ecosystem.
protocols.question_it_answers: How does an AI application obtain structured context, resources, prompts, and tools?

protocols.name: Agent2Agent Protocol
protocols.adoption_evidence: A2A reports 150+ supporting organizations and bindings/SDKs; stable 1.0 announced in 2026.
protocols.question_it_answers: How do independent agents discover each other and delegate/complete tasks?

protocols.name: Agent Client Protocol
protocols.adoption_evidence: Zed announced its ACP registry and bring-your-own-agent support.
protocols.acronym_collisions: Also IBM Agent Communication Protocol (defunct), OpenAI/Stripe Agentic Commerce Protocol, IBM usage claims, and unrelated Agent Control/Context protocols.
protocols.question_it_answers: How do coding agents interoperate with code editors?

protocols.name: IBM Agent Communication Protocol
protocols.status: Defunct as a standalone protocol; merged into A2A
protocols.adoption_evidence: Official repository states ACP is now part of A2A and links its migration material.
protocols.acronym_collisions: Not Zed ACP or OpenAI/Stripe ACP.
protocols.question_it_answers: How did agents, applications, and people exchange multimodal REST messages?

protocols.name: OpenAI/Stripe Agentic Commerce Protocol
protocols.adoption_evidence: The canonical repository says OpenAI and Stripe first implemented it and provides dated stable 2026-04-17 artifacts.
protocols.acronym_collisions: Not Zed ACP or IBM Agent Communication Protocol.
protocols.question_it_answers: How do buyers' agents and merchants conduct deterministic programmatic checkout?

protocols.name: Universal Commerce Protocol
protocols.adoption_evidence: Launch ecosystem named Shopify, Etsy, Wayfair, Target and Walmart; current UCP site publishes the specification.
protocols.classic_web_analog: Commerce API and merchant capability document
protocols.question_it_answers: Can an agent discover products, form a cart, and transact with a merchant interoperably?

protocols.name: Agent Payments Protocol
protocols.adoption_evidence: Google's launch announcement identifies 60+ launch partners; repository is the normative implementation/spec source.
protocols.question_it_answers: Did a user authorize the agent's purchase and is it within its authority?

protocols.name: AP2 Checkout Mandate
protocols.adoption_evidence: It is a specified AP2 object/profile, not an independent protocol; AP2 is the dated launch evidence.
protocols.question_it_answers: What exactly did the user approve for checkout?

protocols.name: x402
protocols.adoption_evidence: The x402 Foundation's 2026 white paper documents the protocol and its agentic-commerce positioning.
protocols.question_it_answers: How can a client pay per HTTP resource or API request, especially with stablecoins?

protocols.name: L402
protocols.adoption_evidence: Lightning Labs documents L402/Aperture as the operational implementation.
protocols.question_it_answers: How can a client pay for and authenticate to a metered resource on Lightning?

protocols.name: Machine Payments Protocol
protocols.adoption_evidence: NOT FOUND
protocols.question_it_answers: How can machines/agents pay programmatically for services?

protocols.name: ERC-8004 Trustless Agents
protocols.adoption_evidence: EIP draft is primary evidence of the published identity, reputation, and validation registry design; independently quantified deployment was not verified from a primary source.
protocols.question_it_answers: Who is an agent and what reputation/validation evidence supports trusting it?

protocols.name: ERC-8183 Agentic Commerce
protocols.adoption_evidence: NOT FOUND
protocols.question_it_answers: How can agent-service jobs use on-chain escrow and proof of completion?

protocols.name: ERC-8226 Regulated Agent Mandate
protocols.adoption_evidence: The EIP pull request records the published proposal/reference work.
protocols.question_it_answers: What scoped, time-bounded and capped authority may a regulated-asset agent exercise?

protocols.name: WebMCP
protocols.status: Draft Community Group Report; not W3C Standards Track
protocols.governing_body: W3C Web Machine Learning Community Group
protocols.adoption_evidence: Chrome's WebMCP documentation describes its implementation/availability and the community-group specification defines the API.
protocols.question_it_answers: What tools can a web page expose to an in-browser AI agent?

protocols.name: NLWeb
protocols.adoption_evidence: Microsoft's public repository is the dated implementation evidence; no independent deployment count verified.
protocols.question_it_answers: How can a site expose a natural-language interface grounded in its structured data?

protocols.name: Anthropic Agent Skills format
protocols.adoption_evidence: Agent Skills is published by Anthropic and documented as supported in OpenAI's skills documentation.
protocols.question_it_answers: How can reusable procedural knowledge and assets be packaged for an agent?

protocols.name: llms.txt
protocols.adoption_evidence: NOT FOUND
protocols.question_it_answers: Where is a concise, structured map of documentation intended for language models?

protocols.name: AGENTS.md
protocols.adoption_evidence: NOT FOUND
protocols.acronym_collisions: AGENTS.md is a repository instruction convention, not agents.txt.
protocols.question_it_answers: What local instructions should a coding agent follow in a repository?

protocols.name: AIPREF Content-Usage attachment
protocols.probe: Inspect Content-Usage response header or robots.txt
protocols.adoption_evidence: IETF's 2026 draft is active work; no deployment quantity is claimed.
protocols.question_it_answers: What uses does a content publisher prefer automated systems make of acquired content?

protocols.name: AIPREF vocabulary
protocols.adoption_evidence: Published as an IETF work-in-progress reference used by the Web Bot Auth registry draft.
protocols.question_it_answers: What controlled values express AI-use preferences?

protocols.name: Text and Data Mining Reservation Protocol
protocols.status: W3C Community Group final report; not a W3C Recommendation
protocols.governing_body: W3C TDM Reservation Protocol Community Group
protocols.adoption_evidence: NOT FOUND
protocols.question_it_answers: Has a rights holder reserved text-and-data-mining rights?

protocols.name: Cloudflare Content Signals Policy
protocols.adoption_evidence: Cloudflare's announcement describes rollout through its customer controls; no independent adoption count is asserted.
protocols.question_it_answers: May accessed content be used for search, AI input, or training?

protocols.name: Web Bot Auth HTTP-signature protocol
protocols.governing_body: IETF Web Bot Auth Working Group
protocols.adoption_evidence: Cloudflare publishes verifier documentation; draft lists public implementations.
protocols.discovery_mechanism: Signature-Agent header and Signature Agent Card
protocols.question_it_answers: Which automated client made this HTTP request, and can the origin verify it cryptographically?

protocols.name: Web Bot Auth Signature Agent Card
protocols.adoption_evidence: The registry draft provides the concrete published card format for Web Bot Auth.
protocols.question_it_answers: What identity, keys, purpose and expected behavior belong to a signed bot?

protocols.name: HTTP Message Signatures
protocols.adoption_evidence: Web Bot Auth explicitly profiles RFC 9421 in the associated draft and Cloudflare verifier documentation.
protocols.question_it_answers: How can HTTP messages have end-to-end component integrity and proof of possession?

protocols.name: Agentic Resource Discovery
protocols.governing_body: Open project / AI Catalog working group
protocols.adoption_evidence: Google announced ARD and AWS published an implementation-oriented ARD post.
protocols.question_it_answers: Where are an organization's discoverable agents, MCP servers, APIs, skills and catalogs?

protocols.name: AI Catalog well-known file
protocols.adoption_evidence: Google's ARD announcement explicitly directs publishers to host ai-catalog.json; it is primary evidence of the well-known artifact.
protocols.question_it_answers: Which AI-capable artifacts and registries does this domain publish?

protocols.name: DNS for AI Discovery
protocols.adoption_evidence: Infoblox and GoDaddy announced support for the open discovery/identity effort.
protocols.question_it_answers: Given a domain, where is its agent endpoint and what protocol does it speak?

protocols.name: Agent Name Service
protocols.probe: Resolve ANS name / associated DNS proof
protocols.adoption_evidence: GoDaddy/Infoblox's support announcement is dated external adoption evidence.
protocols.question_it_answers: What domain-anchored identity belongs to an autonomous agent?

protocols.name: Agent Identity and Discovery
protocols.adoption_evidence: NOT FOUND
protocols.question_it_answers: Where is an agent and how can it be identified from a domain?

protocols.name: Agent Discovery Protocol
protocols.adoption_evidence: NOT FOUND
protocols.question_it_answers: How are agents and their capabilities found through interoperable discovery methods?

protocols.name: Agent Registration and Discovery Protocol
protocols.adoption_evidence: NOT FOUND
protocols.question_it_answers: How can an agent register and expose discovery metadata?

protocols.name: Agent Directory Service
protocols.adoption_evidence: AGNTCY published an ARD/ADS interoperability note; no deployment quantity asserted.
protocols.question_it_answers: Which agents fit a task, where are they, and what evidence describes them?

protocols.name: Open Agentic Schema Framework
protocols.adoption_evidence: Cisco/AGNTCY documents active OASF use and Open Agent Specification support.
protocols.question_it_answers: How can agent identity, capabilities, skills and deployment metadata be described semantically?

protocols.name: Agent-to-UI Protocol
protocols.adoption_evidence: Published v1 specification and multi-renderer ecosystem are documented on the project site.
protocols.question_it_answers: How can an agent describe and stream a framework-neutral UI?

protocols.name: Agent-User Interaction Protocol
protocols.adoption_evidence: The canonical repository publishes integrations and the protocol documentation.
protocols.classic_web_analog: Event stream between application and backend
protocols.question_it_answers: How does an agent stream state, messages and tool activity into a user-facing application?

protocols.name: Open Semantic Interchange
protocols.adoption_evidence: OSI's public site names participating ecosystem organizations and version milestone.
protocols.acronym_collisions: Open Source Initiative is a separate OSI.
protocols.question_it_answers: How can semantic data definitions move across vendors for analytics and agents?

protocols.name: Open Knowledge Format
protocols.probe: Parse OKF markdown and front matter
protocols.adoption_evidence: Google Cloud announced the format and its Knowledge Catalog/Data Product use.
protocols.question_it_answers: How can durable human/agent-readable knowledge be packaged portably?

protocols.name: OpenAI Apps SDK manifests
protocols.adoption_evidence: OpenAI announced developer app submissions with the Apps SDK.
protocols.discovery_mechanism: MCP server tool metadata and component resource metadata
protocols.question_it_answers: How does a ChatGPT-integrated app declare tools and interactive components?

protocols.name: Agentic Advertising Management Protocols
protocols.adoption_evidence: IAB Tech Lab released AAMP 2.3 and describes its pilot/industry program.
protocols.question_it_answers: How do advertising agents plan, negotiate and execute interoperable transactions?

protocols.name: Agentic Real Time Framework
protocols.adoption_evidence: IAB Tech Lab published the v1.0 final material.
protocols.question_it_answers: How can agent services execute reliably inside programmatic advertising infrastructure?

protocols.name: Ad Context Protocol
protocols.adoption_evidence: Protocol documentation and consortium announcement evidence were found; no primary quantified deployment claim retained.
protocols.question_it_answers: How can agents conduct interoperable digital-ad planning and media transactions?

protocols.name: Visa Trusted Agent Protocol
protocols.adoption_evidence: Visa's launch announcement names ecosystem participants and the protocol's purpose.
protocols.question_it_answers: How does a merchant distinguish a legitimate commerce agent from fraudulent automation?

protocols.name: Mastercard Verifiable Intent
protocols.adoption_evidence: Mastercard published the launch explanation; no independent adoption count retained.
protocols.question_it_answers: Can a merchant cryptographically verify the user's specific authorization for an agent transaction?

protocols.name: SPIFFE workload identity for agents
protocols.status: Active base standard; agent application is profiled/proposed
protocols.adoption_evidence: The IETF AI-agent authentication draft explicitly profiles SPIFFE for AI-agent authentication.
protocols.question_it_answers: Which workload/agent instance is making this request?

protocols.name: Workload Identity in Multi-System Environments
protocols.adoption_evidence: IETF WIMSE's active working-group material and the agent-auth draft show its application to agents.
protocols.question_it_answers: How do workloads, including agents, authenticate across platforms and trust domains?

protocols.name: Agent Authorization Grant
protocols.adoption_evidence: The dated IETF draft is existence evidence only; no shipping deployment was verified.
protocols.question_it_answers: How can an autonomous agent obtain delegated OAuth access when browser redirect is unavailable?

protocols.name: Delegated Agent Authorization Protocol
protocols.adoption_evidence: The published August 2026 draft is existence evidence only.
protocols.question_it_answers: How can a principal delegate constrained authorization to an agent?

protocols.name: Agent Authorization Profile
protocols.adoption_evidence: Canonical draft and public reference repository establish proposal activity, not deployment.
protocols.question_it_answers: How can OAuth flows carry agent/task/capability authorization semantics?

protocols.name: Agent Identity Protocol
protocols.adoption_evidence: The 2026-06-09 IETF individual draft is existence evidence only.
protocols.question_it_answers: How can an agent prove decentralized identity and delegation authority?

protocols.name: Agent Transfer Protocol
protocols.adoption_evidence: The IETF draft is existence evidence only.
protocols.question_it_answers: How can an agent be transferred/handed off between systems?

protocols.name: Verified Commerce for Agent Protocols
protocols.adoption_evidence: The 2026-09-04 draft is existence evidence only.
protocols.question_it_answers: How can autonomous agents settle a transaction with evidence of delivery?

protocols.name: Agent Network Protocol
protocols.adoption_evidence: NOT FOUND
protocols.question_it_answers: How can decentralized agents discover, trust and collaborate without a central registry?

protocols.name: Agora Protocol
protocols.adoption_evidence: The project repository and paper demo are published; no independent deployment verified.
protocols.question_it_answers: How can agents exchange scalable structured communications?

protocols.name: Agora commerce protocol
protocols.adoption_evidence: Repository reports a testnet/catalog state but does not provide independently verified adoption.
protocols.acronym_collisions: Distinct from the research Agora Protocol.
protocols.question_it_answers: How can agents discover services and conduct marketplace commerce?

protocols.name: s402
protocols.adoption_evidence: NOT FOUND
protocols.question_it_answers: How can a client discover and satisfy a payment requirement?

not_verified: IBM Agent Commerce Protocol (ACP): no distinct IBM-maintained protocol/specification could be verified. The IBM repository found is a reference implementation of OpenAI/Stripe ACP and UCP, not a separate IBM ACP.
ARD uses /.well-known/ai-catalog.json. No primary specification was found establishing /.well-known/ard.json as the ARD catalog filename.
robots.txt Agentmap directive: treated as an ARD discovery convention, not an independent ratified standard.
Cloudflare pay-per-crawl: a commercial product/program, not a separately verifiable open protocol specification.
DID-based agent identity: W3C DID is a general base standard; the agent-specific profiles below are drafts/proposals, not a single settled DID-for-agents standard.
Several one-off GitHub proposals returned by discovery were excluded because there was no independently dated adoption evidence.
